The aim of this study is to provide accurate spectroscopic parameters and rotational transition frequencies for thioformamide to enable astronomical searches for this molecule using radio telescope arrays at millimeter wavelengths.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00074.S.
the frequency range from 84.1 GHz to 114.4 GHz was fully covered with a spectral resolution of 488 kHz (1.7 to 1.3 km s$^{-1}$).

The interferometric observations achieved an angular resolution (half-power beam width, HPBW) varying between $\sim$0.3$\ensuremath{''}$ and $\sim$0.8$\ensuremath{''}$, with a median value of 0.6$\ensuremath{''}$.
The rms sensitivity ranged between 0.35 mJy beam$^{-1}$ and 1.1 mJy beam$^{-1}$, with a median value of 0.8 mJy beam$^{-1}$.
The rotational spectrum of thioformamide was measured and analyzed in the frequency range 150 to 660 GHz using the Lille spectrometer.
